Every computed picture and video of this wiki has a record on this page: what was computed, how, with which parameters and checks, and the code that produced it.

== How a record works ==
* A record is a section with an anchor <code>num-…</code>; the picture or video links to it with the parameter <code>record</code> of [[Template:Media|Media]].
* It gives the equation, the parameters, the method, the checks, the code and how to run it, and its status.
* The code is in the folder <code>numerics/</code> of the [https://github.com/endipa/endipa.github.io repository] of the wiki, one folder per record, with the output of its checks.

== Records ==
=== Heat versus shear on the torus {{Anchor|num-heat-vs-shear}} ===
{| class="levels"

|-
| Equation || <math display="inline">\partial_t f+\sin y\,\partial_x f=\nu\Delta f</math> on <math display="inline">[0,2\pi)^2</math>, periodic, and the heat equation <math display="inline">\partial_t f=\nu\Delta f</math>; same datum <math display="inline">f_0=\cos x</math>
|-
| Parameters || <math display="inline">\nu=10^{-3}</math>, times <math display="inline">0\le t\le 100</math>; video of 20 s at 24 frames per second, time running uniformly (5 time units per second), last frame held 1.5 s

{{Fold start|kind=note|title=Code}}
<pre data-lang="python">
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Heat equation versus advection-diffusion by a shear flow on the torus [0, 2pi)^2.

    d_t f + sin(y) d_x f = nu (d_xx + d_yy) f,      f(0, x, y) = cos x,

compared with the heat equation (the same without the transport term), whose solution is
exp(-nu t) cos x. The initial datum has zero average in x. It is a single Fourier mode in x,
so f(t, x, y) = Re(g(t, y) e^{ix}) with

    d_t g = -i sin(y) g + nu (d_yy - 1) g,      g(0, y) = 1,

solved by a Fourier method in y with Strang splitting: the transport step is the exact
multiplication by exp(-i sin(y) dt), the diffusion step is exact in Fourier variables.
The L2 norm reported is ||f(t)|| / ||f(0)||, that is the root mean square of |g(t, .)|.

Checks (written to heat-vs-shear-check.txt and heat-vs-shear-check.png):
  * the run is repeated with twice the Fourier modes and half the time step, and the norms are compared;
  * energy balance: ||g(t)||^2 + 2 nu int_0^t ||(d_y g, g)||^2 ds = ||g(0)||^2 (means over y).

The video lasts --duration seconds; frame s in [0, 1] shows t = T (a s + (1 - a) s^2), a = --slow (default 1:
time runs uniformly; a < 1 slows down the start); the last frame is held --hold seconds.

Outputs, in --out: heat-vs-shear.mp4 (video), heat-vs-shear-poster.png (one frame of it),
heat-vs-shear-check.png and heat-vs-shear-check.txt. Needs NumPy, Matplotlib and ffmpeg
(with the libx264 encoder). Run:  python3 heat_vs_shear.py --out ../../wiki/media

Drafted by Claude (AI) on 8 November 2026 for the wiki "Enhanced dissipation for passive
scalars"; record: page Numerical methods, section num-heat-vs-shear.
"""
import argparse
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile

import numpy as np
import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

HEAT_COLOR = "#b4532a"
SHEAR_COLOR = "#1f4e79"


def solve(nu, T, N, dt, frame_times=()):
    """Times, norms ||f(t)||/||f(0)||, energy-balance residuals, and g(t, y) at frame_times."""
    y = 2 * np.pi * np.arange(N) / N
    eta = np.fft.fftfreq(N, d=1.0 / N)              # integer wavenumbers in y
    symbol = eta ** 2 + 1.0                          # symbol of -(d_yy - 1): mode k = 1 in x
    half = np.exp(-nu * symbol * dt / 2)
    transport = np.exp(-1j * np.sin(y) * dt)
    ghat = np.fft.fft(np.ones(N, dtype=complex))
    steps = int(round(T / dt))
    times = dt * np.arange(steps + 1)
    sq = np.empty(steps + 1)                         # mean over y of |g|^2
    dissip = np.empty(steps + 1)                     # mean over y of |d_y g|^2 + |g|^2
    frames, targets, j = [], list(frame_times), 0
    for n in range(steps + 1):
        power = np.abs(ghat) ** 2 / N ** 2           # Parseval: means over y
        sq[n] = power.sum()
        dissip[n] = (symbol * power).sum()
        while j < len(targets) and targets[j] <= times[n] + dt / 2:
            frames.append(np.fft.ifft(ghat))
            j += 1
        if n == steps:
            break
        ghat *= half
        ghat = np.fft.fft(np.fft.ifft(ghat) * transport) * half
    integral = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum((dissip[1:] + dissip[:-1]) / 2) * dt])
    residual = np.abs(sq + 2 * nu * integral - 1.0)
    return times, np.sqrt(sq), residual, frames, y


def field(g, nx):
    """f(x, y) = Re(g(y) e^{ix}) on an nx-by-nx grid (rows: y, columns: x)."""
    step = max(1, len(g) // nx)
    x = 2 * np.pi * np.arange(nx) / nx
    return np.real(g[::step][:, None] * np.exp(1j * x)[None, :])


def draw_frame(path, t, g, nu, times, norms, heat, nx, ymin):
    x = 2 * np.pi * np.arange(nx) / nx
    f_heat = np.exp(-nu * t) * np.cos(x)[None, :] * np.ones((nx, 1))
    f_shear = field(g, nx)
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(11.2, 7.2), dpi=100)
    gs = fig.add_gridspec(2, 2, height_ratios=[3.6, 1.15], hspace=0.3, wspace=0.06,
                          left=0.08, right=0.97, top=0.845, bottom=0.095)
    for col, (data, title) in enumerate([(f_heat, "Heat equation:  $u = 0$"),
                                         (f_shear, r"Shear flow:  $u = (\sin y,\, 0)$")]):
        ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, col])
        ax.imshow(data, origin="lower", extent=[0, 2 * np.pi, 0, 2 * np.pi], cmap="RdBu_r",
                  vmin=-1, vmax=1, interpolation="bilinear")
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=17, pad=8)
        ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
        ax.set_aspect("equal")
    fig.suptitle(r"Same initial datum $f_0 = \cos x$, same diffusivity $\nu = 10^{-3}$"
                 + "        t = %d" % round(t), fontsize=17, y=0.975)
    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :])
    k = np.searchsorted(times, t, side="right")
    ax.semilogy(times, heat, color=HEAT_COLOR, alpha=0.18, lw=2)
    ax.semilogy(times, norms, color=SHEAR_COLOR, alpha=0.18, lw=2)
    ax.semilogy(times[:k], heat[:k], color=HEAT_COLOR, lw=2.4, label="heat equation")
    ax.semilogy(times[:k], norms[:k], color=SHEAR_COLOR, lw=2.4, label="shear flow")
    ax.axvline(t, color="#888888", lw=1)
    ax.set_xlim(0, times[-1]); ax.set_ylim(ymin, 1.5)
    ax.set_yticks([10.0 ** e for e in range(int(np.log10(ymin)), 1)])
    ax.set_xlabel("time  t", fontsize=13)
    ax.set_ylabel(r"$\|f(t)\|\,/\,\|f_0\|$", fontsize=14)
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=11)
    ax.legend(loc="lower left", fontsize=12, frameon=False, ncol=2)
    fig.savefig(path)
    plt.close(fig)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=".", help="folder for the video and the figures")
    ap.add_argument("--nu", type=float, default=1e-3)
    ap.add_argument("--T", type=float, default=100.0)
    ap.add_argument("--N", type=int, default=512, help="Fourier modes in y")
    ap.add_argument("--dt", type=float, default=0.01)
    ap.add_argument("--duration", type=float, default=20.0, help="length of the video in seconds")
    ap.add_argument("--fps", type=int, default=24)
    ap.add_argument("--slow", type=float, default=1.0, help="speed of time at the start, relative to the mean (1: uniform)")
    ap.add_argument("--hold", type=float, default=1.5, help="seconds the last frame is held")
    ap.add_argument("--nx", type=int, default=256, help="pixels per side of each panel")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    os.makedirs(a.out, exist_ok=True)
    s = np.linspace(0, 1, int(round(a.duration * a.fps)))
    frame_times = a.T * (a.slow * s + (1 - a.slow) * s ** 2)
    times, norms, residual, frames, y = solve(a.nu, a.T, a.N, a.dt, frame_times)
    heat = np.exp(-a.nu * times)
    # check: the same run with N doubled and dt halved
    times2, norms2, residual2, _, _ = solve(a.nu, a.T, 2 * a.N, a.dt / 2)
    diff = np.abs(norms2[::2] - norms) / norms2[::2]
    ymin = 10 ** np.floor(np.log10(norms.min()))
    with open(os.path.join(a.out, "heat-vs-shear-check.txt"), "w") as fh:
        fh.write("nu=%g T=%g N=%d dt=%g frames=%d fps=%d\n" % (a.nu, a.T, a.N, a.dt, len(frame_times), a.fps))
        fh.write("final norm: shear %.4e, heat %.4e\n" % (norms[-1], heat[-1]))
        fh.write("max relative difference with (2N, dt/2): %.2e\n" % diff.max())
        fh.write("max energy-balance residual: %.2e (2N, dt/2: %.2e)\n" % (residual.max(), residual2.max()))
        fh.write("decay rate of the shear norm on [T/2, T]: %.4f; nu^(1/2) = %.4f\n" % (
            np.log(norms[len(norms) // 2] / norms[-1]) / (times[-1] - times[len(times) // 2]), np.sqrt(a.nu)))
    # check figure
    fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4), dpi=100)
    ax1.semilogy(times, heat, color=HEAT_COLOR, lw=2, label="heat equation (exact)")
    ax1.semilogy(times, norms, color=SHEAR_COLOR, lw=2, label="shear flow, N=%d, dt=%g" % (a.N, a.dt))
    ax1.semilogy(times2, norms2, color="k", lw=1, ls="--", label="shear flow, N=%d, dt=%g" % (2 * a.N, a.dt / 2))
    ax1.set_xlabel("time t"); ax1.set_ylabel("norm ratio"); ax1.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9)
    ax1.set_title("Norms (log scale)")
    ax2.semilogy(times[1:], diff[1:] + 1e-16, color=SHEAR_COLOR, lw=1.5, label="relative difference of the two runs")
    ax2.semilogy(times[1:], residual[1:] + 1e-16, color="#6b7280", lw=1.5, label="energy-balance residual")
    ax2.set_xlabel("time t"); ax2.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9); ax2.set_title("Checks")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(os.path.join(a.out, "heat-vs-shear-check.png"))
    plt.close(fig)
    # video
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        for i, (t, g) in enumerate(zip(frame_times, frames)):
            draw_frame(os.path.join(tmp, "f%04d.png" % i), t, g, a.nu, times, norms, heat, a.nx, ymin)
        poster = min(range(len(frame_times)), key=lambda i: abs(frame_times[i] - 0.2 * a.T))
        shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(tmp, "f%04d.png" % poster), os.path.join(a.out, "heat-vs-shear-poster.png"))
        subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-loglevel", "error", "-framerate", str(a.fps),
                        "-i", os.path.join(tmp, "f%04d.png"), "-vf", "tpad=stop_mode=clone:stop_duration=%g" % a.hold,
                        "-c:v", "libx264", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
                        "-crf", "26", "-preset", "slow", "-movflags", "+faststart",
                        os.path.join(a.out, "heat-vs-shear.mp4")], check=True)
    print(open(os.path.join(a.out, "heat-vs-shear-check.txt")).read().strip())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
</pre>

=== Alternating shears with random phases {{Anchor|num-alternating-shears}} ===
{| class="levels"
| Produces || the second video on the [[Overview]] (<code>alternating-shears.mp4</code>) and the check figure below
|-
| Equation || <math display="inline">\partial_t f+u\cdot\nabla f=\nu\Delta f</math> on <math display="inline">[0,2\pi)^2</math>, periodic, with <math display="inline">f_0=\cos x</math> and the alternating shears of Pierrehumbert's model: <math display="inline">u=(\sin(y+\varphi_n),0)</math> for <math display="inline">6n\le t<6n+3</math> and <math display="inline">u=(0,\sin(x+\psi_n))</math> for <math display="inline">6n+3\le t<6n+6</math>, the phases independent and uniform on <math display="inline">[0,2\pi)</math>; compared with the steady shear <math display="inline">u=(\sin y,0)</math> and with the heat equation. Both velocity fields have size at most 1.
|-
| Parameters || <math display="inline">\nu=10^{-4}</math>, each shear acting for a time 3, times <math display="inline">0\le t\le 60</math>, phases from the random generator of NumPy with seed 2026; video of 20 s at 24 frames per second, time running uniformly (3 time units per second), last frame held 1.5 s
|-
| Method || Fourier pseudo-spectral method on a <math display="inline">512\times512</math> grid; Strang splitting with time step 0.0125, the transport steps (each row or column shifted, through its Fourier coefficients) and the diffusion steps solved exactly; the steady shear as in the record above
|-
| Checks || with <math display="inline">1024\times1024</math> modes and time step 0.00625 the norms agree to a relative <math display="inline">1.2\cdot10^{-6}</math>; the energy balance <math display="inline">\|f(t)\|^2+2\nu\int_0^t\|\nabla f\|^2ds=\|f_0\|^2</math> holds to <math display="inline">3.5\cdot10^{-6}</math>; time for the norm to halve, for <math display="inline">\nu=10^{-2},10^{-3},10^{-4},10^{-5}</math>: alternating shears 8.8, 16.3, 23.9, 31.7 (the same with twice the modes), an increase of about 7.6 for each factor 10 in <math display="inline">\nu</math>; steady shear 8.6, 20.0, 43.9, 94.9; heat equation <math display="inline">\ln 2/\nu</math>
|-
| Context || Exponential mixing for randomly shifted alternating shears is proved by [[Literature#BCZG2023|Blumenthal, Coti Zelati and Gvalani (2023)]], and dissipation on the time scale <math display="inline">|\log\nu|</math>, with high probability, by [[Literature#CoopermanIyerSon2025|Cooperman, Iyer and Son (2025)]]; whether the parameters used here satisfy their hypotheses has not been checked
|-
| Code || [https://github.com/endipa/endipa.github.io/blob/main/numerics/alternating-shears/alternating_shears.py numerics/alternating-shears/alternating_shears.py] in the repository (Python 3, NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, ffmpeg); <code>python3 alternating_shears.py --out ../../wiki/media</code>, about 15 minutes
|-
| Status || computed by Claude (AI) on 8 November 2026; not yet checked by a human {{Demo}}
|}
{{Media|kind=image|file=alternating-shears-check.png|caption=Left: the norms for <math display="inline">\nu=10^{-4}</math>, with two resolutions for the alternating shears. Right: the time for the norm to halve, against <math display="inline">1/\nu</math>, logarithmic scales.}}

=== A vortex in log-polar coordinates {{Anchor|num-log-polar}} ===
{| class="levels"
| Produces || the video in the note ''Why this domain?'' of [[Couette flow]] (<code>log-polar.mp4</code>) and the check figure below; the same script draws the figure of that note (<code>log-polar-map.svg</code>) from the explicit formulas, without any computation
|-
| Equation || <math display="inline">\partial_t f+V(r)\partial_\theta f=\nu\Delta f</math> in the plane, with <math display="inline">V(r)=1/(1+r^2)</math>; in the coordinates <math display="inline">r=e^s</math> it is <math display="inline">\partial_t f+V(e^s)\partial_\theta f=\nu e^{-2s}(\partial_\theta^2+\partial_s^2)f</math> on <math display="inline">(\theta,s)\in\mathbb{T}\times\mathbb{R}</math>; datum <math display="inline">f_0=\cos(2\theta)\exp(-(s/0.8)^4)</math>. The checks compare with the same equation without the flow (<math display="inline">V=0</math>)
|-
| Parameters || <math display="inline">\nu=10^{-3}</math>, times <math display="inline">0\le t\le 40</math>; video of 15 s at 24 frames per second, time running uniformly, last frame held 1.5 s
|-
| Method || one Fourier mode in <math display="inline">\theta</math>: <math display="inline">f=\operatorname{Re}(g(t,s)e^{2i\theta})</math> with <math display="inline">e^{2s}\partial_t g=-2iV(e^s)e^{2s}g+\nu(\partial_s^2-4)g</math> for <math display="inline">-3.2\le s\le 2.8</math> and <math display="inline">g=0</math> at the two ends; centred second-order differences with 1500 intervals in <math display="inline">s</math>; Crank–Nicolson scheme with time step 0.01
|-
| Checks || with 3000 intervals and time step 0.005 the norms agree to a relative <math display="inline">2.6\cdot10^{-4}</math>; the energy balance <math display="inline">\int|g(t)|^2e^{2s}ds+2\nu\int_0^t\!\!\int(|\partial_s g|^2+4|g|^2)\,ds\,dt'=\int|g(0)|^2e^{2s}ds</math> holds to <math display="inline">1.6\cdot10^{-5}</math> of its initial value; <math display="inline">|g|</math> at the two ends of the grid stays below <math display="inline">2.2\cdot10^{-5}</math>. The norm is that of <math display="inline">L^2</math> of the plane, <math display="inline">\|f(t)\|^2=\int|g(t)|^2e^{2s}ds</math> up to a constant; at <math display="inline">t=40</math> it is 0.105 times its initial value, and 0.852 times without the flow
|-
| Code || [https://github.com/endipa/endipa.github.io/blob/main/numerics/log-polar/log_polar.py numerics/log-polar/log_polar.py] in the repository (Python 3, NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, ffmpeg); <code>python3 log_polar.py --out ../../wiki/media</code>
|-
| Status || computed by Claude (AI) on 10 November 2026; not yet checked by a human {{Demo}}
|}
